key_insight: Photonic variational circuits are trainable when the observable’s variance decays only polynomially, but become impractical when the required measurement precision scales exponentially with system size.
engineering_relevance: This gives a concrete design rule for near-term photonic quantum algorithms: choose low-order photon-number observables or efficient neural-network readouts to keep sampling costs manageable.
method: Defined trainability using the ratio of sample variance to circuit variance.
Analyzed photon-number observables for local loss differences and gradient estimation.
Compared observable families to separate polynomial-scaling regimes from exponentially hard regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic results plus numerically observed polynomial decay of circuit variance, showing fixed-order photon-number polynomials need only polynomially many samples, while high-order polynomials and output probabilities typically need exponentially many.
watch_item: The practical benefit depends strongly on observable choice and measurement efficiency, so implementations that rely on high-order or probability-based readouts may still face prohibitive sampling costs.
paper_title: The trainability of photonic quantum circuits
